The main takeaway from our work is that

the class of Bayesian networks can be viewed as a “natural” class of learning systems with the following key properties: (1) they are based on a simple, transparent probabilistic representation of the data distribution, and (2) their class of induced decision functions can be represented within inner product spaces with a low (up to factor 2) dimension.
Bayesian networks can be viewed as kernel-based systems, which are, however, more expressive and more interpretable than the standard kernel-based learning systems.
the class of decision trees, the class of Bayesian networks and the class of kernel-based learning algorithms are closely related in terms of their representational capabilities.
